source_read: PDF pp. 19-20 (PDFs/MDMA/Madero_2023_PremisePromiseChallenges.pdf): read in full, including the declaration of competing interest and the 10 references; both pages rendered at 110 dpi to fix columns and paragraph breaks. For one cross-check, the MAPP1 abstract (Mitchell et al., 2021) read on nature.com in my own browser tab. Step 1 (blind extraction) not run this round, per the round brief.

design.note: An 'Insights' commentary; narrative-review is the closest schema value. Six paragraphs (three beginning on p. 19, three on p. 20) and 10 references confirmed.

instrument.note: none-applicable with the editors' narrative-review checklist.

key_findings.note: p. 19, 2nd paragraph: Merck 1912, Shulgin 1976, hundreds of therapists (no citation), the night scene, Schedule I in October 1986 'without any convincing academic arguments' (the authors' words, no citation).
3rd paragraph begins at the foot of the left column (MAPS since the early 2000s) and continues in the right column (pooled phase 2 data, Breakthrough designation in 2017, multi-site phase 3).

The finding is accurate; its note needs one fix. The source does give a time reference, 'after completing treatment', which also points to completers as the denominator; what it lacks is a count, a week and the placebo-arm figure. As a completers' figure, two thirds agrees with MAPP1's 28 of 42 (67%) carried by cl_mdma_ptsd_efficacy; it is higher than the share of everyone randomized (61%, editors' calculation in that claim). The description of the design and of the CAPS-5 result follows the MAPP1 abstract's own wording.

key_findings.correction: The authors write that the safety profile of MDMA appears favourable because it did not induce adverse events of abuse potential, suicidality or QT prolongation. The sentence carries no citation of its own; it follows the sentence citing Mitchell et al. (2021) and repeats almost word for word that trial's abstract. How these events were assessed is not described.
key_findings.note: 'No source is cited' is literally true of the sentence but misleads: the statement is the trial authors' own summary, repeated without appraisal (MAPP1 abstract read on the publisher's page). Its wording means no excess over placebo, not absence: the MAPP1 anchors in cl_mdma_ptsd_adverse_events record suicidality events of special interest in 3 of 46 on MDMA and 5 of 44 on placebo.

p. 19, 3rd paragraph, right column: USA, Canada and Israel; top-line results meeting primary and secondary endpoints (no reference); NDA planned for the 3rd quarter of 2023; approval 'very likely' within the next year and a half; therapists trained in seven named countries; a phase 3 trial in 2024; EMA approval possibly from 2026.
p. 20, 5th paragraph: the risks paragraph opens by calling MDMA-AT, like almost any effective approved treatment, inherently risky, which presupposes efficacy and approval.

Last sentence of the 5th paragraph; every figure matches. The source calls Avanceña et al. a cost-effectiveness analysis; its own title (reference list) calls it a modelling study of costs and health benefits of expanded access.
6th paragraph, foot of the left column.
6th paragraph, continued at the top of the right column.

reporting_issues.note: Corrected issue: the safety statement has no citation of its own and does not say how such events were looked for; it follows the citation of Mitchell et al. (2021) and repeats that trial's abstract, so it is the trial authors' own conclusion restated without appraisal rather than an unsourced claim. Consequence unchanged: it cannot be used as evidence on adverse events; the trial report, its adverse-event methods and the critiques are needed.
The two commentaries may be naming different steps (Schedule I classification here, criminalization in Nutt and de Wit); neither cites a document.

Corrected issue: as much as two thirds of the MDMA arm no longer meeting PTSD criteria 'after completing treatment' is given without a count, a week or the placebo-arm figure; the phrase points to completers. Consequence: not citable as a remission or loss-of-diagnosis rate; as a completers' share it is consistent with the trial report, and the between-arm difference and the share of everyone randomized must come from the trial report.

risk_of_bias.note: I agree with every domain and the overall.

domains.note: The trial is summarized in its own abstract's words, which is the opposite of appraisal.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: Low is right on the domain's wording (none of the 10 references is by either author). The substantive tie, O.A. being a principal investigator in the programme whose trial is the piece's main evidence, is a funding-and-interests flag, as the card records it.

domains.domain: Balance of evidence on the benefits and risks of MDMA-assisted therapy
domains.note: Some concerns rather than high is defensible because risks, therapist training, hype and lowered journal standards are acknowledged.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. One citation fix in 'claimed': 'in August 2024 the FDA rejected the application (Mahase, 2024)' cites a source that gives no date for the decision; the month comes from Marseille and Mitchell (2025, p. 1, citing CNN), while Mahase supports 'by 13 August 2024, before the retractions'. Either cite both or write 'by August 2024'.

missed: Field correction (sample.selection_effects): Sessa et al. (2019) is not shown by this source to be 'by the sponsor's investigators'; its reference lists Sessa, Higbed and Nutt. Only Mithoefer (2017), the MAPS treatment manual, is a sponsor document on the source's own evidence.

The 3rd paragraph's account of MAPP1 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-site; significant attenuation in CAPS-5 compared with placebo; no adverse events of abuse potential, suicidality or QT prolongation) closely follows the trial's own abstract (publisher HTML). The commentary adds a forecast but no appraisal; the interpretation-gap field can say so.

The economic figures come from a model whose authors (Avanceña, Kahn, Marseille; reference list) include the first author of the 2025 critique in this batch; that critique does not cite Avanceña et al. (2022) among the authors' own earlier models (it cites Marseille et al., 2020 and 2022). The card's funding note already makes the link through Marseille's 2025 declaration; the cost claim's 'earlier model with an overlapping author' is right.
